newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: Opposition parties score well in Macedonian poll.
newsitem.headline: Opposition parties score well in Macedonian poll.

text.p: Partial returns showed Macedonian opposition parties leading the ruling Social Democrats in several major towns after municipal polling at the weekend.

A strong showing by the opposition would deal a serious setback to the Social Democrats because both government and opposition treated the local contests like a national plebicite in the former Yugoslav republic.
By late Monday, the opposition alliance led by the conservative VMRO-DPME claimed victory in nine municipalities.
The alliance said it was leading in four major towns and the two largest districts in the capital Skopje.
Political analysts said opposition parties hoped to use the strong local vote as a lever to force the government of Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski out of power.
Even the Social Democrats conceded that the results would bolster the opposition's position.
"On the local level the opposition now has the opportunity to fight for early parliamentary elections," the general secretary of the Social Democratic Alliance, Ljupco Popovski, said on state radio.
Partial returns indicated most of the 124 municipalities would have to hold run-off elections to decide the outcome.
The counting also had not taken account of allegations by the opposition of fraud and widespread reports of irregularities in electoral lists.
European observers monitoring the polling said earlier that 25 percent of voters could not cast their ballots because they were not on electoral lists.
The 12-member Council of Europe delegation said it visited 96 polling stations and found registration problems in almost every case, particularly in Albanian-dominated western districts.
The observers, however, offered no general conclusion about the legitimacy of the polling.
The Social Democrats had won at least 12 councils, although its candidate for mayor of the capital Skopje was trailing in third place.
One diplomat said he was surprised by the strength of the anti-government vote.
"This is not a rout," he said. "But it is certainly a slap in the face for (prime minister) Crvenkovski."

VMRO and its allies boycotted the 1994 parliamentary elections and has no parliamentary representation. Earlier this year the government foiled a VMRO bid to force early elections with a petition of over 200,000 signatures.

The VMRO campaigned for an end to the Social Democrats' sweeping free-market economic reforms, which have been plagued by charges of corruption. VMRO also said it wants a more cautious approach to economic reform and it advocates closer ties with its old Eastern Bloc allies.

The opposition has also urged a tougher line in Macedonia's dispute with Greece over its name. Greece argues that Skopje's claim to "Macedonia" as an official national title implies a territorial claim over its northern province of the same name.
